answers.question: When a cashier records a payment for a patient bill in the billing app, what happens from the button click in the UI down to the database write? Walk me through it.

paragraphs.text: A payment typed by a cashier travels as one HTTP POST from the browser to the OpenMRS REST API, and the server does the whole write inside a single database transaction: it loads the bill, attaches the payment to it, recalculates the bill's status, and saves. Two repositories are involved: the React microfrontend `openmrs-esm-billing-app` (what the cashier sees) and the Java module `openmrs-module-billing` (the REST endpoints and the data model).
## 1. The cashier fills in the form

The invoice page `Invoice` reads the bill with `useBill` and renders the `Payments` panel, passing the bill, a `mutate` refetch function and an `onFinalizeBill` callback [1]. Inside `Payments` the cashier picks a payment mode (e.g. cash, mobile money), an amount and an optional reference number, all bound through react-hook-form controllers to the `payment.method`, `payment.amount` and `payment.referenceCode` fields [2]. The dropdown is populated by `usePaymentModes`, which calls `GET /ws/rest/v1/billing/paymentMode` [3].

Validation is a Zod schema on the `Payments` component: the method is required, the amount must be positive and must not exceed the amount still due (net amount minus already tendered) [4]. Note that a bill in `PENDING` status (not yet finalized) shows a "Finalize this bill before recording a payment" empty state instead of the form, and the Process Payment button is hidden while the bill is pending [5].
## 2. The button click

The button labelled "Process Payment" calls `handleProcessPayment` and is disabled until a method and amount are present and the form is valid [6]. The handler sends three fields and no more: `instanceType` (the selected payment-mode UUID), `amountTendered` (what the cashier typed) and `amount` (the bill's total) [7], matching the `PaymentRequestPayload` type [8].

`processBillPayment` turns that into `POST /ws/rest/v1/billing/bill/{billUuid}/payment` with a JSON body [9]. The base path comes from `apiBasePath`, which is the framework's REST base plus `/billing/` [10].

On success it shows a success snackbar, resets the form, refreshes the bill via the `mutate` it was given, and revalidates the patient's payment-status cache key; on failure it shows an error snackbar with the server's message [11].
## 3. The server side

A useful thing to notice: this is a `POST` to the *bill's* `payment` sub-resource, so the REST layer creates a new `Payment` child under the existing bill rather than editing the bill as a whole. `PaymentResource` declares itself a sub-resource at path `payment` under `BillResource` [12].
The three body fields are bound by `@PropertySetter` methods before `save` runs:

| JSON field | Setter | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `instanceType` | `setPaymentMode` [13] | resolves the `PaymentMode` by UUID, throws `ObjectNotFoundException` if unknown |
| `amount` | `setPaymentAmount` [14] | converts to `BigDecimal` |
| `amountTendered` | `setPaymentAmountTendered` [15] | converts to `BigDecimal` |

`cashier` is also a settable field, but the UI never sends it, because `save` fills it in from the authenticated session: `ProviderUtil.getCurrentProvider()` looks up a `Provider` by the logged-in user's person [16]. If the user is not linked to a provider, the request fails with "The authenticated user is not associated with a Provider and cannot process payments." [17].
`save` then does three things: gets the parent `Bill` from the delegate, calls `bill.addPayment(delegate)`, and calls `service.saveBill(bill)` [18].
## 4. Status recalculation on the entity
`Bill.addPayment` puts the payment in the bill's payment set, points the payment back at the bill, and calls `synchronizeBillStatus()` [19]. That method is where the business rules live:

- If the bill is in a refund state (`REFUND_REQUESTED`, `REFUNDED`, `PARTIALLY_REFUNDED`) it leaves the status alone [20].
- If an approved discount no longer matches the line items ("discount drift"), it deliberately keeps the bill `POSTED` for manual review rather than marking it paid [21].
- Otherwise, if total payments now cover the amount after discount, the bill becomes `PAID` and every non-voided, non-refunded line item is marked `PAID`; if not, the bill stays `POSTED` [22].
## 5. The database write

`BillServiceImpl.saveBill` is annotated `@Transactional`, so everything above happens in one transaction and is committed at the end [23]. It delegates to `HibernateBillDAO.saveBill`, which is a single `saveOrUpdate` on the bill [24]. Because the bill's `payments` set is mapped with `cascade="all-delete-orphan"` [25], saving the parent bill also inserts the new child payment — that is why the resource only saves the bill and never saves the payment directly.

Hibernate translates the in-memory `Payment` into an `INSERT` into the `cashier_bill_payment` table: `bill_id`, `payment_mode_id`, `amount`, `amount_tendered`, `provider_id` (the cashier), plus the standard creator/date/uuid audit columns [26]. The JPA entity class for it is `Payment` [27]. Any updated `status` on the bill is written to `cashier_bill` in the same transaction.
## Things worth knowing

- The amount the cashier types is `amountTendered`; the separate `amount` field is sent as the bill's total. Both are stored on the payment row.
- Authorization is OpenMRS session-based (the cashier is derived from the authenticated user's provider record), and the module declares the resource as supported for OpenMRS `2.0 - 2.*` [12]. I did not read a privilege check specific to this endpoint, so I cannot say which privilege guards it.
- After the payment, the SPA may also call `updateBillVisitAttribute` to flip the visit's "pending payment" attribute to false; that is a second, independent POST to the visit attribute endpoint [28].

What I did not verify: the `openmrs-module-fhir2` repository plays no part in this path as far as I read, and I did not inspect the REST framework's own request-handling code (it lives in the external `webservices.rest` module, not in these repositories), so the exact point at which authentication and transaction boundaries are applied around `PaymentResource` comes from reading the resource class and its `@Transactional` service calls, not from the dispatcher itself.
</answer>
